newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom ends bourse five pct down.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom ends bourse five pct down.

text.p: Shares in newly-floated German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom fell over five percent by the bourse close on Tuesday, with dealers blaming profit-taking for the fall.

Telekom shares, which traded for the first time on Monday in Europe's biggest initial public offering, lost 1.83 marks ($1.21) to end down at 32.07, near the day low of 31.95 but still well above the issue price of 28.50 marks.

Volumes in the market debutant were strong, with some 11.6 million shares changing hands in bourse dealings. In computer trade, the stock fell to 31.82 marks on trade of some 14.2 million shares by 1300 GMT.
"Telekom has been kicked downwards," said one dealer.

Dealers said there had been strong demand on Monday from institutional investors, who had not received as many shares as they would have liked in the heavily oversubscribed flotation. But they said players were now taking profit in the stock.
Investors were divided over whether Telekom would stablise around current levels or try to climb higher, possibly touching 36 marks.
Meanwhile, the DAX index, in which Telekom is now weighted at 4.5 percent, ended largely flat at 2,764.08.
